cues: Opens with a note on the empty workspace and stated assumptions, then ends with targeted open questions that 'would change the design'. This suggests a procedure of grounding in context and surfacing assumptions.
A 'Core idea' summary comes first, followed by explicit numbered design principles and a 'Biggest risks' section. The structure is disciplined and consistent.
It has a phased roadmap with 'Done when' exit criteria, plus explicit goals and out-of-scope lists. This is typical of a structured planning template.
It includes a build-vs-buy section and ties mitigations to named risks. That breadth is deliberate, but a strong unguided model could also produce it.

The content is very detailed and polished (specific GitHub headers, the lethal trifecta, promotion thresholds). That points to a strong model, and I can't say whether a methodology was involved, so my confidence is moderate.
